quote: (General American) IPA(key): /hʌ/, [hʌ̃], /hə/, [hə̃]
note: A candidate; the parent may prefer U. The RP line is «(Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /hʌ/, [hʌ̃]». There are two grounds, and neither is a non-English segment. (a) [hʌ̃] and [hə̃] have a nasalized vowel with no nasal consonant to cause it. (b) /hʌ/ ends a word with a stressed checked vowel. v1 treated ugh's «Note: may be nasalized.» as allophonic. If that stands, ground (a) falls here too and only (b), a phonotactic ground, remains.
